question.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-2,1)$, $P(3,-1,2)$ and $Q(4,2,0).$
question.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-2,1⟩,\,p=⟨3,-1,2⟩,$ and $q=⟨4,2,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,-1,2⟩-⟨1,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨4,2,0⟩-⟨1,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,4,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+5j+5k \\  & =⟨-5,5,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ & =⟨3,-1,2⟩\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,5,5⟩ & =-10 \\ -5x+5y+5z & =-10 \\ -5x+5y+5z+10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
